For Bangladeshi students planning to study abroad in 2027 and beyond, Germany, Poland, Hungary, Malaysia, Italy, France and Turkey are worth comparing as potentially affordable destinations. However, costs and opportunities vary by university, course, city and individual circumstances. Germany may offer good value through public higher education, while Poland can provide relatively affordable study options in Europe. Malaysia is another destination worth considering for its English-taught programmes and comparatively manageable living costs. Hungary and Italy may become particularly attractive when students secure suitable scholarships.

This guide breaks down the real costs, the trade-offs, and the countries that make the most sense for Bangladeshi students who want an international degree without taking on an unrealistic financial burden.

Quick answer: Which are the cheapest countries for Bangladeshi students?

If you want a short list first, these are the most practical options:

  • Germany - excellent value, very strong for engineering and technical subjects, but the proof-of-funds requirement is high
  • Poland - one of the cheapest countries to study in Europe for international students, with lower living costs than much of Western Europe
  • Hungary - affordable in its own right and even better if you qualify for scholarship support
  • Malaysia - low overall cost, familiar environment, and a wide range of English-medium programmes
  • Italy - affordable public universities and useful scholarship opportunities in some regions
  • France - still viable for budget-conscious students, though fee structures need to be checked carefully
  • Turkey - often overlooked, but a sensible option for students prioritising affordability

If your main priority is finding a lower overall study budget, Malaysia and Poland are useful starting points for comparison. Germany may also offer excellent long-term academic value, particularly through public universities. However, the most affordable option depends on your chosen programme, tuition fees, living expenses, scholarship eligibility and other required costs.

What makes a country truly affordable?

Many articles focus only on tuition fees when comparing affordable study destinations. However, the cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students are not necessarily those with the lowest university fees.

For Bangladeshi students, planning your study budget from Bangladesh requires considering five important factors:

1. Tuition fees

Tuition is a major expense, but it represents only part of the overall cost of studying abroad. Fees vary by country, university, programme and qualification level. Students should compare published tuition fees and any additional university charges before choosing a destination.

2. Cost of living

Accommodation, food, transport, utilities, phone bills and health insurance can sometimes cost more than tuition. Living expenses also vary considerably between cities, so comparing realistic monthly budgets is essential.

4. Part-time work and post-study options

Permitted part-time employment and post-study opportunities can influence a country's overall value. However, working conditions, permitted hours and post-study residence options differ between destinations and may depend on individual circumstances. Students should check official rules and avoid relying on potential employment income to cover essential study expenses.

5. Subject fit and degree quality

Affordable tuition offers limited value if a programme does not match your academic background or career goals. Consider university recognition, course content, teaching quality and future opportunities when comparing destinations.

Ultimately, when deciding which country is best for Bangladeshi students, affordability should be measured through total study costs, academic suitability and relevant entry requirements, rather than tuition fees alone.

1. Germany: the best value for serious students

Germany remains one of the most attractive answers to the question of the cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students, especially for students focused on long-term return rather than just first-year cost.

Many public universities in Germany offer bachelor's and selected master's programmes without tuition fees, although students generally pay a semester contribution. However, tuition fees may apply to certain programmes and institutions, including non-EU students at public universities in Baden-Württemberg and selected universities in Bavaria.

Students should review DAAD's guidance on tuition and living costs in Germany alongside the latest fees published by their chosen university. Compared with some other popular study destinations, these arrangements can make Germany an attractive option for Bangladeshi students seeking affordable higher education.

Why Germany works

  • strong public universities
  • excellent reputation in engineering, IT, natural sciences, and applied fields
  • many English-taught master’s programmes
  • clear post-study opportunities
  • good long-term career value

Typical cost

A practical student budget is usually around €900 to €1,200 per month, depending on the city. Smaller cities are noticeably cheaper than Munich, Frankfurt, or Hamburg.

Best for

  • engineering
  • computer science
  • data and analytics
  • environmental science
  • applied sciences

What to watch

One important consideration for Bangladeshi students planning to study in Germany is understanding the financial requirements for international education. For 2026, official German guidance specifies €11,904 as the standard annual blocked-account amount for students using this method to demonstrate sufficient financial resources. Recognised scholarships and certain other officially accepted financial arrangements may also be considered.

As requirements can change, students planning a 2027 intake should review the latest official German government guidance on studying in Germany and confirm the relevant financial requirements before finalising their study plans.

2. Poland: low-cost Europe without Western European prices

Poland is one of the most practical options for Bangladeshi students seeking an affordable European degree. Students exploring public university options in Poland may find a good balance between tuition fees, living expenses and academic opportunities.

Although Poland may not have the same international reputation as Germany in every subject, it offers recognised higher education institutions, relatively manageable living costs and a growing selection of English-taught programmes. This makes it worth considering among the cheapest countries to study in Europe for international students.

Why Poland works

  • relatively affordable tuition fees at selected universities
  • lower living costs than many Western European destinations
  • a wide range of English-taught degree programmes
  • public and private university options across different subjects
  • practical study opportunities for Bangladeshi students with a limited budget

Typical cost

For international students planning to study in Poland, indicative expenses include:

  • Tuition fees: Approximately €2,000 to €6,000 per year for many fee-paying programmes, although specialised courses may cost more.
  • Living costs: Around €450 to €800 per month as a practical planning estimate, depending on the city, accommodation and lifestyle.

According to Poland's official Study in Poland tuition fee guidance, fees vary by university and programme. The official cost of living guide also illustrates lower-cost student budgets, particularly for those using university accommodation.

These factors make Poland a competitive option for students considering which country is best for Bangladeshi students in Europe on a modest budget. However, actual expenses should always be confirmed with the chosen institution.

Best for

  • engineering
  • business and management
  • information technology (IT)
  • logistics and supply chain management
  • selected health and medical programmes

What to watch

University quality, programme accreditation, tuition fees and admission requirements can vary significantly. Bangladeshi students should check the recognition of their qualifications, language requirements and current institutional policies before applying.

Students planning for the 2027 intake should also review the latest official admission guidance for international students, as qualification recognition and entry requirements may change.

3. Hungary: one of the smartest scholarship-led options

Hungary is an attractive option for Bangladeshi students seeking affordable higher education in Europe. With relatively manageable tuition fees, living costs and a growing selection of English-taught programmes, it offers opportunities across several academic disciplines.

Hungary becomes particularly appealing when scholarships are available. Programmes such as Stipendium Hungaricum can significantly reduce education expenses for eligible students, making it worth exploring when comparing the cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students.

Why Hungary works

  • relatively affordable tuition fees and living costs
  • a wide range of English-taught programmes
  • a central European location
  • scholarship opportunities for eligible international students

Typical cost

A reasonable planning range is:

  • Tuition fees: €2,500 to €8,000 per year for many programmes, although specialised degrees may cost more
  • Living costs: €450 to €800 per month, depending on the city, accommodation and lifestyle

These figures are indicative rather than fixed rates. Students should compare university-specific fees and use the official Study in Hungary cost-of-living guide when preparing their budget.

Best for

  • public health
  • agriculture
  • business
  • engineering
  • international relations

What to watch

Scholarship availability can make a substantial difference to the total cost of studying in Hungary. The Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship offers tuition-free education, a monthly contribution towards living expenses, accommodation support and medical insurance for eligible recipients.

Bangladeshi students should review the latest official scholarship requirements and explore additional scholarship opportunities for Bangladeshi students in Europe before making financial commitments.

4. Malaysia: an affordable option for many Bangladeshi students

Malaysia is one of the most practical destinations for Bangladeshi students seeking affordable international education. Exploring public universities in Malaysia can help students compare tuition fees, English-taught programmes and overall study costs before choosing an institution.

Malaysia can offer a comparatively manageable study budget, while its multicultural environment and familiar food options may make the transition easier for many Bangladeshi students. However, actual expenses depend on the university, programme, accommodation and location.

Why Malaysia works

  • comparatively affordable tuition fees at selected public universities
  • wide availability of English-taught programmes
  • potentially lower living costs than many Western study destinations
  • multicultural environment and familiar lifestyle options
  • a range of undergraduate and postgraduate study opportunities

Typical cost

According to Education Malaysia's official study cost guide, indicative annual tuition fees for international bachelor's degree students include:

  • Public universities: US$2,500 to US$5,000 per year
  • Private institutions: US$6,000 to US$9,500 per year
  • Living costs: Approximately US$300 to US$700 per month as an initial planning estimate, depending on the city, accommodation and lifestyle

These figures are estimates rather than guaranteed fees. Students should also account for accommodation deposits, medical insurance, travel, administrative charges and applicable taxes. Malaysia introduced a 6% Sales and Service Tax (SST) on tuition fees for international students from 1 July 2025, so applicants should confirm whether this is included in their university's quoted fees.

Malaysia remains worth considering for Bangladeshi students comparing the cheapest countries to study abroad, particularly when affordable tuition and living expenses are priorities.

Best for

  • business and management
  • hospitality and tourism
  • computing and information technology
  • media and communication
  • foundation and pathway programmes

What to watch

University quality, tuition fees and programme recognition can vary considerably. Before choosing an institution, students should check whether their intended qualification appears in the official Malaysian Qualifications Register (MQR) and confirm the latest entry requirements directly with the university.

Students should also avoid assuming that part-time employment will cover their living expenses. International student employment is subject to restrictions and official approval, with permitted work generally limited to eligible semester breaks or holidays. Comparing programme quality, total costs and current official requirements is essential before making a decision.

5. Italy: affordable public education with scholarship potential

Italy is an attractive option for Bangladeshi students seeking affordable higher education in Europe. It combines relatively low public university tuition fees with recognised institutions and scholarship opportunities that may significantly reduce overall study expenses.

Although Italy is not the cheapest destination in every category, it can offer excellent academic value when university fees, living costs and available scholarships are considered together.

Why Italy works

  • relatively affordable public universities
  • respected institutions across several academic disciplines
  • regional and university scholarship opportunities for eligible students
  • a practical European study option compared with some higher-cost destinations

Typical cost

Students planning to study in Italy can use the following indicative budget:

  • Tuition fees: Approximately €900 to €4,000 per year at many public universities, although fees may be lower or higher depending on the institution, programme and applicable reductions.
  • Living costs: Around €700 to €1,100 per month, depending on the city, accommodation and lifestyle.

According to the official Study in Italy guidance, tuition fees vary by university, degree programme and relevant financial circumstances. Some institutions also offer exemptions or reduced contributions to eligible students.

Best for

  • architecture
  • economics
  • design
  • engineering
  • humanities

6. France: still possible on a budget, but more nuanced than it sounds

France is often considered among the cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students, particularly those interested in affordable public universities and recognised European qualifications. However, the actual cost depends on the institution, degree level, location and applicable tuition fee policy.

Public higher education in France can offer good value compared with several other popular study destinations. However, non-EU students, including those from Bangladesh, may be subject to higher tuition fees. Some universities offer exemptions or reduced fees for eligible students, making it important to compare individual institutions before deciding.

Why France works

  • internationally recognised universities and qualifications
  • public higher education with government-subsidised tuition
  • English-taught programmes in selected disciplines
  • scholarship and tuition fee exemption opportunities
  • strong academic options in arts, business, social sciences and public policy

Typical cost

For Bangladeshi students, a realistic study budget should consider the following indicative costs:

  • Bachelor's tuition: €2,902 per year for non-EU students subject to differentiated public university fees in 2026/27.
  • Master's tuition: €3,950 per year under the same fee arrangements.
  • Living costs: Approximately €700 to €1,200 per month, depending on the city, accommodation and lifestyle.

These tuition figures apply to relevant public higher education programmes, and eligible students may qualify for exemptions. Private institutions and specialised courses may charge considerably more.

Students can review the latest Campus France tuition fee guidance and official living cost information when estimating their expenses.

Best for

  • arts and design
  • social sciences
  • business and management
  • international relations
  • humanities

What to watch

France can be an affordable option, but tuition fees and living expenses vary significantly between institutions and cities. Scholarship availability, fee exemptions and programme requirements should be confirmed directly with the university. Students planning to study in 2027 should also check the latest published fees rather than relying solely on previous academic-year figures.

7. Turkey: affordable, practical, and often underrated

Turkey is often overlooked when comparing the cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students. However, it can be a practical choice for those seeking affordable international education, particularly at selected public universities.

Why Turkey works

  • comparatively affordable tuition at selected public universities
  • a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes
  • English-taught courses at certain institutions
  • scholarship opportunities for eligible international students
  • potentially lower living costs than many Western European destinations

Typical cost

Tuition fees and living expenses vary significantly depending on the university, programme, language of instruction and city. Selected public universities may offer lower-cost options, while private institutions and specialised courses can be considerably more expensive.

Eligible students can also explore Türkiye Scholarships, which may cover tuition fees, accommodation, health insurance and other specified expenses for successful applicants. Scholarship availability and eligibility conditions should be checked through the official programme.

Best for

  • engineering
  • business
  • international relations
  • health sciences at selected institutions
  • theology and related subjects

What to watch

Which country is best for Bangladeshi students?

The best country for Bangladeshi students depends on tuition fees, living costs, academic goals, scholarship opportunities and future career plans. Each destination offers different advantages.

Choose Germany for long-term academic value

Germany offers respected public universities and strong opportunities in engineering, IT and applied sciences. However, students should consider living expenses and official financial requirements.

Choose Poland for affordable education in Europe

Poland is among the cheapest countries to study in Europe for international students, offering relatively affordable tuition, manageable living costs and English-taught programmes.

Choose Malaysia for lower overall study costs

Malaysia is a practical choice for Bangladeshi students seeking affordable tuition, English-medium education and comparatively low living expenses.

Choose Hungary for scholarship opportunities

Hungary offers affordable programmes and scholarships such as Stipendium Hungaricum, which can reduce education costs for eligible students.

Choose Italy or France for subject-specific opportunities

Italy and France offer recognised universities, diverse programmes and potential scholarships. Costs vary by institution, city and fee policy.

Ultimately, which country is best for education for Bangladeshi students depends on individual budgets, subject preferences, academic requirements and career goals. Compare total costs and official requirements before making a decision.

Cheapest countries to study in Europe for international students

For Bangladeshi students focused on Europe, the strongest affordable options are usually:

Germany

Best overall value, especially for high-quality public education.

Poland

Often one of the cheapest and most practical European choices.

Hungary

Strong for scholarship-minded students.

Italy

A very good option where public tuition and aid line up well.

France

Worth considering if the specific fee structure is favourable.

If your search is specifically for the cheapest countries to study in Europe for international students, Germany and Poland usually lead the shortlist, but Hungary and Italy often become equally compelling in the right circumstances.

Cheapest English-speaking countries for international students

This query comes up often, but it needs a distinction.

If you mean native English-speaking countries, the affordable options are limited. Countries like the UK, Ireland, Australia, Canada, and New Zealand are generally not low-cost destinations for Bangladeshi students.

If you mean countries with English-taught programmes, then the picture is better. The strongest affordable options usually include:

  • Malaysia
  • Germany
  • Poland
  • Hungary
  • Italy in selected universities
  • France in selected programmes

In practical terms, many Bangladeshi students now get better value by choosing an affordable country with English-medium study rather than insisting on a traditional English-speaking destination.

Study Abroad Requirements for Bangladeshi Students: What Matters Most

Before choosing a destination, consider these essential factors:

  • Academic eligibility: Check university entry requirements and recognised qualifications.
  • Financial requirements: Compare tuition fees, living expenses and any required proof of funds.
  • Course suitability: Consider programme accreditation, scholarships and long-term career opportunities.

The real cost of studying abroad

The total cost of studying abroad includes much more than tuition. This is where students either plan well or get caught out.

Accommodation

Usually the biggest monthly expense. Shared housing can reduce costs significantly.

Food

Cooking at home almost always makes a meaningful difference.

Transport

Manageable in many student cities, but still part of the monthly budget.

Health insurance

Mandatory in many destinations and often underestimated.

Books, supplies, and admin fees

Not the biggest expense, but they add up.

Emergency budget

A smart study plan always includes some buffer. Budgets with no margin tend to collapse under pressure.

Scholarships that can change everything

Bangladeshi students should explore:

  • Hungary: Stipendium Hungaricum, offering tuition coverage and contributions towards living costs.
  • Europe: Erasmus Mundus scholarships for selected master's programmes.
  • Italy and France: Regional, government and university scholarships.
  • Turkey: Türkiye Scholarships for eligible international students.
  • Malaysia: Institution-based scholarships and merit-based awards.

How to shortlist your best options

If you are comparing too many countries, simplify the process.

Germany is best if:

  • you want strong long-term value
  • your field is technical or applied
  • your family can handle the proof-of-funds requirement

Poland is best if:

  • you want Europe at a manageable total cost
  • you need lower living expenses
  • you are prepared to research universities carefully

Malaysia is best if:

  • you want the lowest realistic total budget
  • you prefer an easier adjustment
  • you value affordability over brand prestige

Hungary is best if:

  • scholarships are a major part of your plan
  • you want a lower-cost European route
  • you have found suitable English-medium programmes

Italy or France are best if:

  • your subject fit is particularly strong
  • you want a respected European degree
  • you are prepared for more paperwork and institution-level research

Common mistakes Bangladeshi students make

Choosing by tuition alone

Following outdated blog advice

Ignoring the city

The same country can feel affordable in one city and expensive in another.

Choosing the wrong course for the wrong reason

Assuming every English-medium course offers the same value

Quality, recognition, and outcomes vary sharply.

Frequently asked questions

Which are the cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students?

Which country is best for Bangladeshi students?

Germany is often the strongest long-term option, Poland is excellent for affordable Europe, and Malaysia is one of the best choices for lower overall cost and easier adjustment.

Which country is best for Bangladeshi students in Europe?

For most students, Germany and Poland are the strongest European options. Hungary and Italy are also very competitive, especially where scholarships or lower public-university fees apply.

What is the cheapest country to study abroad for Bangladeshi students if I want English-taught courses?

Malaysia is often the easiest affordable answer. Germany, Poland, and Hungary also offer good English-medium options, especially at postgraduate level.

Final thoughts

The phrase cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students sounds simple, but the decision rarely is.

For one student, Germany will be the best option because the academic return is worth the upfront financial proof. For another, Poland will make more sense because it keeps both tuition and living costs under control. For many families, Malaysia will be the most practical answer because the total cost is easier to manage. Others will find that Hungary, Italy, France, or Turkey fit better once scholarships, subject choice, and long-term plans are considered properly.

The most practical way to compare the cheapest countries to study abroad for Bangladeshi students is to consider total education costs, current official entry requirements and long-term academic value together. For students starting their study abroad journey from Bangladesh, comparing these factors alongside programme quality and scholarship opportunities can make it easier to build a realistic shortlist.
